title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Desk Guide: History Window for Holiday Pay after an Earlier Claim Closes
content:
For a holiday-pay report on Unemployment Benefit Claims, the history window — the months counted back from the handling date over the certifications, by week ending date, of the claimant's most recent earlier claim of the same program — follows how recently that earlier claim closed. The date read is the closed date on the earlier claim.

| Earlier claim's closed date | History window |
|---|---|
| No more than 30 days before the handling date (recent closure) | 12 months (the recent-claim window) |
| More than 30 days but no more than 180 days before the handling date | 6 months (the mid window) |
| Any other case, including an earlier claim with no closed date | 3 months (the standard window) |

## Boundary days

| Days from the closed date to the handling date | Window |
|---|---|
| 30 | 12 months |
| 31 | 6 months |
| 180 | 6 months |
| 181 | 3 months |

### Hypothetical case

An earlier claim closed 45 days before the handling date: the certifications read are those whose week ended within the 6 months before the handling date.
